newsitem.title: GERMANY: BHF Bank downgrades Veba to hold from buy.
newsitem.headline: BHF Bank downgrades Veba to hold from buy.

text.p: Germany's BHF Bank said on Thursday that it had downgraded its recommendation for German diversified utility Veba AG to hold from buy, and lowered its earnings per share (EPS) outlook for the group.
For 1997, BHF has lowered its EPS outlook to 5.60 marks from 5.90 marks and from 6.20 marks from 6.65 marks in 1998.
Veba's EPS in 1996, calculated by the DVFA analysts method, rose to 5.04 marks from 4.33 marks, a figure which BHF utilities analyst Thomas Deser said in a report was somewhat below expectations.
The report said that the expected rise in earnings at Veba in coming years encouraged a positive stance on Veba shares.
However, a slowdown in the dynamic earnings growth seen in recent years and less spectacular growth in earnings in the first part of the year meant a more careful approach was necessary.
